t.en: Peter the Great founded the city on 27 May 1703 (16 May old style) with the Peter and Paul Fortress. It was Russia’s capital until 12 March 1918, when Lenin moved the government to Moscow. It became Petrograd in 1914, Leningrad on 26 January 1924 and Saint Petersburg again on 6 September 1991. The siege of 1941–1944 lasted 872 days and killed more than a million civilians.
t.ru: Пётр I основал город 27 мая 1703 года (16 мая по старому стилю), заложив Петропавловскую крепость. До 12 марта 1918 года, когда Ленин перевёл правительство в Москву, он был столицей России. В 1914 году город стал Петроградом, 26 января 1924 года — Ленинградом, 6 сентября 1991 года вновь Санкт-Петербургом. Блокада 1941–1944 годов длилась 872 дня и унесла жизни более миллиона мирных жителей.

t.en: Moscow is first mentioned in the chronicles in 1147. Italian masters raised the Kremlin’s brick walls and towers for Ivan III in 1485–1495. After the fire of 1812 a commission rebuilt the city; the Bolshoi Theatre opened in 1825. Lenin moved the government here from Petrograd on 12 March 1918. The city passed a million people at the census of 1897 and thirteen million at the census of 2021.
t.ru: Москва впервые упомянута в летописи под 1147 годом. В 1485–1495 годах итальянские мастера возвели для Ивана III кирпичные стены и башни Кремля. После пожара 1812 года город отстраивала особая комиссия; в 1825 году открылся Большой театр. 12 марта 1918 года Ленин перевёл сюда правительство из Петрограда. По переписи 1897 года в городе жило больше миллиона человек, по переписи 2021 года — больше тринадцати миллионов.

t.en: Novgorod is first mentioned under 859 in the Nikon Chronicle and under 862 in the Primary Chronicle. At its height, around the late 14th century, it had an estimated 20,000–30,000 people. Saint Sophia Cathedral was built in 1045–1050. The Millennium of Russia monument was unveiled in the Detinets in 1862.
t.ru: Новгород впервые упомянут в Никоновской летописи под 859 годом, в «Повести временных лет» — под 862-м. В пору расцвета, около конца XIV века, в нём жило, по оценкам, 20–30 тысяч человек. Софийский собор построен в 1045–1050 годах. Памятник «Тысячелетие России» открыт в детинце в 1862 году.

t.en: Pskov first appears in the chronicle under 903, when Igor of Kiev married Olga, a local woman. Its Krom was walled from the 13th century onwards. The Trinity Cathedral was founded in 1138 and rebuilt in the 1690s. In 1510 the city had more than 30,000 people.
t.ru: Псков впервые упомянут в летописи под 903 годом, когда Игорь Киевский взял в жёны псковитянку Ольгу. Кром обносили стенами начиная с XIII века. Троицкий собор заложен в 1138 году и перестроен в 1690-х. В 1510 году в городе жило более 30 тысяч человек.

t.en: The Lvov Chronicle dates Vladimir’s founding by Vladimir Monomakh to 1108; the city’s 2005 charter names 990 instead, so the date is disputed. Andrey Bogolyubsky built the Golden Gate (1158–1164) and the Dormition Cathedral (1158–1160). Vsevolod the Big Nest added the Cathedral of Saint Demetrius (1194–1197).
t.ru: Львовская летопись относит основание Владимира Владимиром Мономахом к 1108 году; устав города 2005 года называет 990 год, так что дата спорна. Андрей Боголюбский построил Золотые ворота (1158–1164) и Успенский собор (1158–1160). Всеволод Большое Гнездо возвёл Дмитриевский собор (1194–1197).

t.en: Suzdal is first mentioned in the chronicles under 1024. Yury II built the Cathedral of the Nativity in 1222–1225; it was rebuilt in 1528–1530. The Monastery of Saint Euthymius was founded in 1352, and its walls went up in 1640–1644. Two Suzdal monuments joined UNESCO’s White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal in 1992.
t.ru: Суздаль впервые упомянут в летописи под 1024 годом. Юрий II построил Рождественский собор в 1222–1225 годах; в 1528–1530 годах его перестроили. Спасо-Евфимиев монастырь основан в 1352 году, его стены возведены в 1640–1644 годах. В 1992 году два суздальских памятника вошли в список ЮНЕСКО «Белокаменные памятники Владимира и Суздаля».

t.en: Tradition holds that Yaroslav the Wise founded the city in 1010, while he ruled Rostov; the date cannot be fully proved. The Transfiguration Monastery was rebuilt in stone in 1506–1516. The Church of Elijah the Prophet was completed in 1650 and painted around 1680. The Volkov Theatre dates from 1750.
t.ru: По преданию, Ярослав Мудрый основал город в 1010 году, когда княжил в Ростове; доказать эту дату нельзя. Спасо-Преображенский монастырь отстроен в камне в 1506–1516 годах. Церковь Ильи Пророка завершена в 1650 году и расписана около 1680-го. Волковский театр ведёт историю с 1750 года.

t.en: Kostroma’s official founding year is 1152, attributed to Yury Dolgoruky; scholars think the site may be older. The Epiphany Cathedral (1559–1565) was its first stone building. Boris Godunov had the Ipatiev Monastery rebuilt in stone. In 1910 Prokudin-Gorsky photographed the Church of the Resurrection on the Debre.

Борис Годунов отстроил Ипатьевский монастырь в камне. В 1910 году Прокудин-Горский снял церковь Воскресения на Дебре.

t.en: Kazan celebrated its millennium in 2005; the date rests partly on a Czech coin found in the Kremlin. The first chronicle mention is in 1391, and New Kazan became the capital of the Kazan Khanate in 1438. Ivan IV took the city after a siege in 1552. The Annunciation Cathedral was built in 1561–1562.
t.ru: Казань отметила тысячелетие в 2005 году; дата отчасти опирается на чешскую монету, найденную в Кремле. Первое летописное упоминание относится к 1391 году, а в 1438 году Новая Казань стала столицей Казанского ханства. В 1552 году город после осады взял Иван IV. Благовещенский собор построен в 1561–1562 годах.

t.en: Tver’s foundation year is officially accepted as 1135, under its city charter. Its wooden kremlin is first recorded in a chronicle of 1317 and burned in the fire of 1763. From 20 November 1931 to 17 July 1990 the city was called Kalinin. The White Trinity Church dates from 1564.

t.en: Smolensk is first mentioned under 863 in the Ustyug Chronicle. Its stone kremlin was built in 1597–1602 under Fyodor Kon. The Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth took the fortress in 1611 after a twenty-month siege. In August 1812 Napoleon’s army and the Russian army fought here; losses were estimated at 30,000 men.
t.ru: Смоленск впервые упомянут в Устюжской летописи под 863 годом. Каменный кремль построен в 1597–1602 годах под руководством Фёдора Коня. В 1611 году, после двадцатимесячной осады, крепость взяла Речь Посполитая. В августе 1812 года здесь сошлись армия Наполеона и русская армия; потери оценивают в 30 тысяч человек.

t.en: Cossacks under Danilo Chulkov founded Tobolsk in 1587. In 1708 it became the capital of the new Siberia Governorate. Its stone kremlin, the only one in Siberia, was built in 1699–1717. In August 1917 the Provisional Government sent Nicholas II and his family here; in spring 1918 the Bolsheviks moved them to Yekaterinburg.
t.ru: Тобольск основали в 1587 году казаки во главе с Данилой Чулковым. В 1708 году он стал столицей новой Сибирской губернии. Каменный кремль — единственный в Сибири — построен в 1699–1717 годах. В августе 1917 года Временное правительство отправило сюда Николая II с семьёй; весной 1918 года большевики перевезли их в Екатеринбург.

t.en: In 1661 Yakov Pokhabov built an ostrog near the site. The stone Church of the Saviour was laid in 1706 in the fort’s north-western corner. Many Decembrists were exiled here after the revolt of 1825. The fire of 4–6 July 1879 destroyed three-quarters of the city, about 4,000 houses.

t.en: Kyiv, today the capital of Ukraine, was the chief city of Kievan Rus’. Tradition dates its founding to 482. By 1000 it had about 45,000 people. Saint Sophia Cathedral was built under Yaroslav the Wise; its foundation is dated 1011, 1017 or 1037. Batu Khan’s army destroyed the city in 1240, and in 1246 perhaps 2,000 people remained.
t.ru: Киев — ныне столица Украины — был главным городом Древней Руси. Предание относит его основание к 482 году. Около 1000 года в нём жило примерно 45 тысяч человек. Софийский собор построен при Ярославе Мудром; его закладку относят к 1011, 1017 или 1037 году. В 1240 году войско Батыя разорило город; в 1246 году в нём оставалось, по оценке, около 2 тысяч жителей.

notes: Coverage: Saint Petersburg 16 population points, 24 landmarks, 36 photographs; Moscow 14 points, 23 landmarks, 27 photographs (below the 30–40 asked). The other cities have 2–8 points, 2–5 landmarks and 0–2 photographs. Photographs are all before 1917; 1917 photographs from the Bulla category were left out.

Commons could not be opened from this session. WebFetch returned ‘url_not_found’ for every commons.wikimedia.org page tried (category and file pages). Wikipedia ‘File:’ pages for Commons files failed the same way, and the shell has no web access. So no file page was checked, and every ‘lic’ is a category pattern, not a reading. Check each file page before display.

Where the file names come from: (a) titles and URLs of Commons search results; (b) the download.osmand.net mirror of three Commons category pages: Photographs of Saint Petersburg by Karl Bulla (https://download.osmand.net/wiki/Category:Photographs_of_Saint_Petersburg_by_Karl_Bulla), Moscow on photochrome prints (https://download.osmand.net/wiki/Category:Moscow_on_photochrome_prints) and 19th century photochrome prints of Russia (https://download.osmand.net/wiki/Category:19th_century_photochrome_prints_of_Russia). The mirror gave names only, read by a summarising fetcher. A name could be mistyped or out of date. Two that looked garbled were left out: one starting ‘Осква.’ and one with a Cyrillic ‘с’ in ‘Riсker’.

Page URLs seen in search results: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Egorov_bathhouse_in_Saint-Petersburg,_Russia,_about_1910.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Larinsky_Hall_of_Imperial_Public_Library_Photograph_by_K_K_Bulla_1900s.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alexander's_Column,_St._Petersburg,_Russia-LCCN2001697508.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_the_Great_Place,_St._Petersburg,_Russia-LCCN2001697500.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alexander_Theatre,_St._Petersburg,_Russia-LCCN2001697501.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Carrick_King_Frost.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:La_Lavra,_Kiev,_Russia,_(i.e.,_Ukraine)-LCCN2001697429.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_%E2%80%A6trialsanderrors_-_Sergei_Prokudin-Gorskii,_Church_of_the_Resurrection_in_the_Grove,_Kostroma,_Russian_Empire,_1910.jpg; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%D0%9C%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B2%D0%B0._%D0%92%D0%B8%D0%B4_%D0%BD%D0%B0_%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%BB%D1%8C_(%D1%81_%D0%9C%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B2.%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0)._1898%D0%B3_big_486981883185_e1t.jpg. Every other ‘page’ value was built from the exact file name in Commons’ canonical form (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File: + the name with underscores, UTF-8 percent-encoded) and was not opened.

Licence patterns. Karl Bulla died on 28 November 1929 (en.wikipedia, Karl Bulla); his category also holds work by his studio. Photochroms: the Library of Congress record for the Photoglob Co. set of Russian views (LOT 13419, ca. 1890–ca. 1900) gives the publisher as Photoglob Co., the Detroit Publishing Co. as US distributor, and the rights as ‘No known restrictions on publication’ (https://www.loc.gov/item/2001696357/). The files named LCCN2001697xxx come from the LoC Photochrom print collection, and the ‘P.Z.’ and ‘Moscou … LOC ppmsca’ files are Photoglob Zürich prints. Prokudin-Gorsky died in 1944 and William Carrick in 1878; neither date was checked this turn. One Moscow file (‘Москва. Вид на Кремль (с Москв.моста). 1898г …’) has no known author, so its public-domain status is the weakest.

Photographs: the year of an undated photochrom is set to 1895 (the LoC range is ca. 1890–1900), and the year of a ‘1900s’ Bulla photograph to 1905; the captions give the range. Two captions are inferred. ‘Moscou. Le Kremlin LOC ppmsca.52725’ is captioned from its Photoglob twin (‘Кремль и Москворецкий мост … 52725u’). The Egyptian Bridge collapse is dated 1905 from general knowledge. Carrick is represented by one file, ‘Carrick King Frost.jpg’; its subject and its year (set to 1870) were not checked.

Photographs are thin for the twelve cities. On Commons, Prokudin-Gorsky files are mostly named ‘Gorskii 0NNNNu.jpg’ or ‘Prokudin-Gorskii-NN.jpg’, so the name does not give the subject, and the file pages could not be opened to identify them. Next time, from a session that can reach Commons, mine these categories: Photos of Tobolsk Governorate by Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky; Photo of Saint Petersburg Governorate by Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky; Photos of European Russia by Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky; Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky; History of Kostroma; Ipatiev Monastery; 19th century photochrome prints of St. Petersburg / of Moscow / of Ukraine; Saint Petersburg in the 1890s; William Carrick (all seen as Commons search results).

Population is thin in places. Smolensk has 2 points: the historical table of the en article did not come through, and its 2010 figure is from the en list. Suzdal has 3, one of them a 2015 estimate. Kyiv has 3 estimates for the Rus’ period. Tobolsk has 4, and its article gives 100,352 for both 2010 and 2021. The ru.wikipedia pages «Население Москвы» and «Список городов России с населением более 100 тысяч человек» failed to load, so Moscow before 1897 rests on rounded statements in en «Moscow» and ru «История Москвы». The en «Moscow» table notes that its figures may reflect changes of boundary (e.g. the 2012 expansion). In each pop row a fifth element ‘U’ marks an estimate, or a figure that differs between sources (the label says how).

PastVu: https://pastvu.com/ was opened (title ‘Retro photos of mankind’s habitat.’). It is a JavaScript app, and its served HTML shows no map-link format. The ‘Using the Map’ guide (https://docs.pastvu.com/en/guides/map) confirms a button that copies ‘URL to the current map position’ but does not give its parameters. The pattern given (g=lat,lon & z=zoom) is from prior knowledge, so test one link before shipping. A documented and verified alternative is the API (https://docs.pastvu.com/en/dev/api): https://api.pastvu.com/api2?method=photo.giveNearestPhotos&params={"geo":[LAT,LON],"limit":12} (optional distance in metres, year, year2). It returns cid, file, title, year, geo and dir; the image is https://img.pastvu.com/d/<file>, and photo pages look like https://pastvu.com/p/<cid> (seen in search results, e.g. https://pastvu.com/p/980238). The rights of PastVu photographs vary: link out only, never copy.
